title: Archives
subtitle: zip, tar, gzip — pack, extract, stream, and search compressed data

cards.meaning: Pack+compress ZIP / bundle many files (optional gzip) / compress one stream
cards.example: zip -r out.zip dir/; tar -cvzf a.tar.gz dir/; gzip file
cards.notes: Memory hook: tar = glue files. gzip = squeeze one stream. tar.gz = glue then squeeze. zip = both in one format.

cards.meaning: Pack a folder into a ZIP (recursive; store relative paths)
cards.notes: -r = recursive. Course example uses -rp for a folder. Common with Windows/Java.

cards.meaning: Extract ZIP contents into the current directory
cards.notes: Also lists/tests archives. See man unzip for more flags.

cards.meaning: Create a tar archive (verbose, file name last)
cards.notes: c = create, v = verbose, f = file. -f must be last among these because the filename follows it.
x = extract. Can restore individual files from the archive too.

cards.meaning: List contents of a tar archive
cards.notes: t = list. No extract — just see what is inside.
z = filter through gzip. Memory cluster: cvf / xvf / tf / cvzf.

cards.front: tar cf - dir1 | (cd dir2 && tar xf -)
cards.meaning: Copy a tree via stdout/stdin — no .tar left on disk
cards.example: tar cf - dir1 | (cd dir2 && tar xf -)
cards.notes: - as archive name = stdout (create) or stdin (extract). Local tree copy through a pipe.

cards.meaning: Pack on host1 → through your machine → unpack on host2
cards.example: ssh root@host1 "cd /src && tar -cf - ." | ssh root@host2 "cd /dst && tar -xf -"
cards.notes: Same - pipe idea over two SSH sessions. No intermediate archive file required.

cards.meaning: Compress to stdout; leave the original file alone
cards.notes: Default gzip file replaces file with file.gz. Use -c or -k to keep the original.

cards.meaning: Append another gzip member (works, usually worse ratio)
cards.notes: Prefer cat file1 file2 | gzip > foo.gz — one gzip of both files compresses better.

cards.meaning: One gzip of concatenated input — better compression than two >> members
cards.notes: Better than gzip -c a > foo.gz then gzip -c b >> foo.gz.

cards.meaning: Print decompressed content without leaving a decompressed file
cards.notes: zcat and gunzip -c are equivalent here. Peek at .gz data.
Search logs that stay compressed on disk — no manual gunzip first.
